title: Establishing a surface and camera reference in Hogwarts

scenes.title: hogwarts-stair-reference
lines: After comparing surfaces in four games, establish an observation reference in this2022 Hogwarts showcase. The character in yellow climbs stairs below bright windows. Identify the clothing, windows and shaded wall.

scenes.title: hogwarts-arch-camera
lines: Outside, the same clothing is framed by sky and stone pillars. The camera looks up at the towers, then follows the stairs. The character remains the reference, while background and viewing direction change. Record those conditions when comparing images.

scenes.title: hogwarts-terrace-reference
lines: At the balustrade, nearby stone and distant landscape share one image. Red identifies the nearby rail; another color identifies the distant view. Looking down changes occlusion too. This is why brightness comparisons need the observation position as well.

scenes.title: hogwarts-brazier-view
lines: The camera turns around the character near a burning brazier. Follow the flame, clothing and stone floor separately. A bright flame and a lit surface are different observation targets; one region alone does not describe the entire image.

scenes.title: hogwarts-hall-camera
lines: Back in the hall, the character appears dark against a bright window. Turning the camera moves the window and carved decorations within the image. Identify the window, clothing and stairs in that order. A consistent reference makes color and exposure changes easier to read.

scenes.title: hogwarts-courtyard-ui
lines: Finally, approach a character beneath the tree. The Talk prompt identifies an interaction target; our red mark identifies the clothing under observation. Keep the game's instructions distinct from our comparison marks.
